title: 1998 HMMT February Algebra Problem 1
statement: The cost of 3 hamburgers, 5 milk shakes, and 1 order of fries at a certain fast food restaurant is \(\$ 23.50\). At the same restaurant, the cost of 5 hamburgers, 9 milk shakes, and 1 order of fries is \(\$ 39.50\). What is the cost of 2 hamburgers, 2 milk shakes ,and 2 orders of fries at this restaurant?

solutions.text:
Let \(H=\) hamburger, \(M=\) milk shake, and \(F=\) order of fries. Then \(3 H+5 M+F=\$ 23.50\). Multiplying the equation by 2 yields \(6 H+10 M+2 F=\$ 47\). Also, it is given that \(5 H+9 M+F=\$ 39.50\). Then subtracting the following equations

\[\begin{aligned}
& 6 H+10 M+2 F=\$ 47.00 \\
& 5 H+9 M+F=\$ 39.50
\end{aligned}\]

yields \(H+M+F=\$ 7.50\). Multiplying the equation by 2 yields \(2 H+2 M+2 F=\$ 15\).
